title: This week in 5 numbers: Remote work may be hurting college grads
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week — including how artificial intelligence will affect customer service jobs.

title: OSHA inspector sues DOL, alleging manager sexually harassed her
summary: Employers may be automatically liable when supervisors harass employees, the government has previously warned.

title: Menopause leave is ‘a missed opportunity’ for employers, NFP says
summary: Menopause symptoms typically occur during a woman’s peak career years and can contribute to lower productivity, greater absenteeism and even workforce attrition, one report found.

title: Front-line managers are key to making improvement plans work, survey finds
summary: Managers who oversee front-line workers are best suited to know what’s happening on the front line, why it’s happening and where to focus next, according to a SafetyCulture report.

title: Half of current customer service jobs will be lost to AI by 2030, Forrester predicts
summary: “There are humans today doing jobs that don't require the level of intelligence that a human has,” Forrester’s Max Ball said. “That work is going to go away.”

title: HR teams say they continue to rely on manual workarounds despite new HCM systems
summary: Companies invest in complex programs designed to facilitate daily tasks, but poor implementation leads to few workers actually using them, a Strada report indicates.

title: Amazon not liable for contractor’s medical emergency, district court rules
summary: While courts have said there may be a “strong moral and humanitarian obligation” to inspect situations that set off an alarm, there is no legal requirement to do so, per the order.

title: Why has youth unemployment risen so dramatically? It may not be AI.
summary: Artificial intelligence can’t explain the disparity in hiring between generations, an analysis from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York noted.

title: Illinois pushes back against Trump in move to ban disparate impact bias
summary: Practices such as strength tests or criminal background checks have been the subject of disparate impact challenges in the past.

title: AI is coming for the workplace — and HR is in the driver’s seat
summary: HR pros are laser focused on training and worker wellness amid tumultuous change.
